title: Paolo Banchero Orlando Magic 2025-2026 Game Worn Icon Edition Jersey
description_block: This away ‘Icon Edition’ jersey was worn in the 2nd Half by Paolo Banchero on October 30, 2025 when the Orlando Magic played the Charlotte Hornets. Banchero finished with 20 points, 9 rebounds, 9 assists, and 2 steals. The Magic beat the Hornets, 123-107. Paolo Banchero was selected with the first overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft by the Orlando Magic following a standout season at Duke University. A versatile and well-rounded forward, Banchero is known for his ability to score from all areas of the floor, rebound effectively, and create for his teammates. Since entering the league, Banchero has rapidly established himself as one of the premier young stars in the NBA. He was named the 2022–23 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year and was a unanimous selection to the NBA All-Rookie First Team. In 2023–24, he earned his first All-Star selection after averaging 22.6 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 5.4 assists per game, becoming the youngest player in Magic history to lead the team in all three categories. During the 2024–25 season, Banchero elevated his play once again, averaging 25.9 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 4.8 assists per game. He became one of only three players aged 22 or younger in league history to surpass 4,000 points, 1,300 rebounds, and 900 assists within his first three seasons, joining LeBron James and Luka Dončić. Banchero also recorded a career-high 50-point game and helped lead Orlando back to postseason contention. At the time of cataloging, Banchero holds career averages of 22.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game. He is a one-time NBA All-Star, the 2022–23 NBA Rookie of the Year, and a member of the 2022–23 NBA All-Rookie First Team. This jersey has been photomatched by PSA.

title: Jimmy Butler Golden State Warriors 2025-2026 Game Worn Icon Edition Jersey
description_block: This away ‘Icon Edition’ jersey was worn in the 2nd Half by Jimmy Butler on December 28, 2025 when the Golden State Warriors played the Toronto Raptors.  Butler finished with 19 points, 6 rebounds, and 5 assists. The Warriors lost to the Raptors, 141-127. Jimmy Butler is one of the most polarizing players in the NBA. His presence on the court has both endeared and frustrated fans and players alike. Butler's play style is characterized by his relentless intensity, versatility, and defensive prowess. He's a crafty driver who excels at attacking the basket and drawing fouls and possesses a smooth mid-range jumper. His improved three-point shooting makes him a scoring threat from all 3 levels on the floor. His offensive impact isn’t all about scoring- he's also an excellent facilitator, using his vision and basketball IQ to create opportunities for his teammates. Butler truly shines on the defensive end. He's a tenacious defender who takes pride in shutting down his opponents with his combination of size, strength, and quick hands. His defensive versatility allows him to guard multiple positions, making him a valuable asset for any team's defensive scheme. As the last player picked in the 1st round of the 2012 NBA Draft, nobody expected Butler to emerge into the superstar he has become. He’s earned 6 trips to the All-Star Game, been named to 5 All-NBA teams, and 5 NBA All-Defensive teams, and won the 2015 Most Improved Player award. After spending time with the Chicago Bulls, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Philadelphia 76ers, he has taken his career to the next level with the Miami Heat. This includes appearances in 2 NBA Finals, including one run as an 8 seed, and another Eastern Conference Finals appearance. His ability to flip a switch in the playoffs, highlighted by his career-high 56-point effort against the Milwaukee Bucks, has earned him the nickname ‘Playoff Jimmy.’ At the time of cataloging, Butler has career averages of 18.4 points per game, 5.4 rebounds per game, and 4.4 assists per game. This jersey has been photomatched by Sotheby’s Photomatching.

description_block: This home ‘Statement Edition’ jersey was worn by Jalen Williams on December 31, 2025 when the Oklahoma City Thunder played the Portland Trail Blazers. Going Deeper | Jalen Williams Jalen Williams’ 2024–25 season marked his arrival as one of the league’s most versatile two-way forces and a foundational pillar of the Oklahoma City Thunder’s championship run. Emerging as a dynamic secondary creator alongside MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams earned his first All-Star selection, a spot on the 2025 All-Defensive Second Team, and his first All-NBA honor, being named to the All-NBA Third Team. His blend of size, skill, and efficiency helped propel Oklahoma City to its first championship in Oklahoma City and second in franchise history. Williams’ development into a legitimate two-way star was defined by his ability to impact the game on all fronts. He took major strides as an on-ball defender, often drawing the toughest perimeter assignments, while evolving into one of the league’s most efficient wing scorers. His improved playmaking and decision-making allowed him to seamlessly shift between primary initiator and off-ball weapon, giving the Thunder one of the most flexible offensive engines in the NBA. Drafted 12th overall in the 2022 NBA Draft out of Santa Clara University, Williams entered the league as a late-rising prospect known for his length, feel for the game, and positional versatility. He quickly validated Oklahoma City’s confidence in him, earning 2023 NBA All-Rookie First Team honors after a standout debut season that showcased his defensive instincts and scoring potential. Over the following seasons, Williams continued to elevate his game. He became a fixture in Oklahoma City’s core, consistently improving his scoring efficiency, expanding his perimeter shooting, and refining his ability to create advantages off the dribble. By 2025, he had solidified his status as one of the league’s premier young wings, capable of filling multiple roles on both ends of the floor. At the time of cataloging, Williams holds career averages of 18 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 4.5 assists per game. This jersey has been photomatched by Sotheby’s Photomatching.
